book.title: Blue Skies over Beijing: Economic Growth and the Environment in China
book.summary: How individuals and the government are changing life in China's polluted cities Over the past thirty years, even as China's economy has grown by leaps and bounds, the environmental quality of its urban centers has precipitously declined due to heavy industrial output and coal consumption. The country is currently the world's largest greenhouse-gas emitter and several of the most polluted cities in the world are in China. Yet, millions of people continue moving to its cities seeking opportunities. Blue Skies over Beijing investigates the ways that China's urban development impacts local and global environmental challenges.

argument.statement: China’s urban development and economic growth have degraded environmental quality in its polluted cities, driven by heavy industrial output and coal consumption, even as millions continue moving for opportunities.

book.rationale: The book focuses on the environmental challenges posed by economic growth in China, examining the interplay between urban development, environmental quality, and societal demands for cleaner living conditions.
